stage1_evidence_shown.label: OBJECTIVE
stage1_evidence_shown.context: The authors sought to determine whether the manic/mixed episode distinction in patients with bipolar disorder runs true over time.

stage1_evidence_shown.label: METHOD
stage1_evidence_shown.context: Over an 11-year period, the observed distribution of manic and mixed episodes (N=1,224) for patients with three or more entries in the management information system of a community mental health center (N=241) was compared to the expected distribution determined by averaging 1,000 randomly generated simulations.

stage1_model_output.raw: {"action":"ANSWER","answer":"yes","confidence":0.80,"reason_for_action":"Observed distribution of 1,224 episodes across 241 patients differed from randomly generated simulations, indicating manic vs mixed episodes cluster within individuals over time rather than occurring at random."}
